decisionMeaning: This manifest records intended connector/platform scope separately from what has actually been accepted on a real host. Platform and architecture arrays are target scope, not tested support. It is not a claim that any row has passed. Every row carries `acceptanceEvidence`; a row whose evidence is empty is an open sales gate, and deploy/native/run-support-matrix.mjs fails closed on it. `additionalInterceptionPoints` lists sold points beyond a row's primary input and output point; Product approved (2026-09-30) selling pre-prompt protection for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and OpenClaw and OpenClaw's pre-model post-tool-output quarantine, and deploy/native/verify-interception-matrix.mjs accepts such an entry only where a real-host acceptance record makes that point enforced. Those records cover linux/x64, a development build and a scripted mock model only.

rows.tamperResistance: host-mediated hook; in-process errors emit an explicit deny, but a disabled hook is fail-open and a hook process killed before it writes a verdict is fail-open (observed on Claude Code 2.1.282)
knownBypasses: Running the model against a file or shell channel the harness does not route through PreToolUse
Direct network access that never constructs a tool call
A UserPromptSubmit hook process killed before it answers cannot block the prompt (host behaviour); only the prompt text is inspected
unobservedActions: Same-turn blocking with a real (non-scripted) model; the real-host record uses a scripted mock model
Behaviour when the host vendor ships a new hook schema

rows.tamperResistance: handled hook failures return deny and managed entries request failClosed: true; real-host enforcement of timeout or process termination remains unverified
installPath: .vsix install via MDM or the extension gallery
knownBypasses: Tools executed outside the extension host (an external terminal)
unobservedActions: Headless agent enforcement coverage on a real Cursor host
A new Cursor version that changes the tool API
Real-host confirmation that failClosed and explicit-deny responses are enforced for preToolUse/MCP events

rows.tamperResistance: in-process plugin callback; a removed plugin means no interception at all
knownBypasses: Plugin removed or the gateway started without it

Pre-model tool-output quarantine needs plugins.entries.aidr-openclaw.enabled: true and the embedded runner; the Codex harness relay and after_tool_call alone do not keep a tool result from the same-turn model

The before_agent_run prompt gate runs only in the embedded and CLI runners (not the Codex or Copilot harnesses), and a non-bundled plugin needs plugins.entries.aidr-openclaw.hooks.allowConversationAccess: true
unobservedActions: Same-turn model blocking through a running gateway (only the embedded `agent --local` runner is recorded)

rows.tamperResistance: in-process plugin; a removed plugin means no interception at all
knownBypasses: Plugin removed or the CLI invoked with the plugin path overridden
Provider streams that bypass the plugin's tool boundary
chat.message prompt protection inspects the user's own text parts only; synthetic parts OpenCode generates (such as attached file contents) are not inspected
unobservedActions: Cases that require a live model provider credential (the real-host record uses a scripted mock model)
Interactive TUI presentation of a blocked prompt

rows.tamperResistance: native PreToolUse and UserPromptSubmit hooks; the host fails open on a crashing or untrusted hook, so the connector maps ask to an explicit deny and answers its own internal errors with a deny or block
installPath: register its PreToolUse and UserPromptSubmit command handlers in ~/.codex/config.toml or ~/.codex/hooks.json and review trust in Codex /hooks
uninstallPath: remove only the AIDR PreToolUse and UserPromptSubmit handlers from ~/.codex/config.toml or ~/.codex/hooks.json
knownBypasses: Host fails open when hook execution is unavailable
No output-side (pre-model) interception exists for this host
The packaged matcher covers Bash and apply_patch only; MCP and other local function tools do not invoke the AIDR hook
Hosted and specialized tool paths may bypass the host tool-hook path

Prompt protection needs the UserPromptSubmit handler registered and trusted separately; an untrusted, crashed or timed-out prompt hook lets the prompt through, and codex exec shows no reason text for a blocked prompt
unobservedActions: Verification against a Codex release newer than 0.141.0
Host-level tamper resistance (for example a patched host binary)
